An Overview of Sentinel Hub, and how developers can contribue to it. Build the Source Code Getting started with building and testing Sentinel core Commands overview of the main commands of Sentinel Hub Key Management Managing keys via CLI and advanced operations such as multisig wallets Set up a Full Node Participate in the network as public rpc or choose to validate
To compile the source code of Sentinel HUB into a binary, two essential steps are necessary: installing Go and executing the build process.
Install Go by following instructions there. Verify the installation by typing go version in your terminal. go version You should receive this output: go version goX.X.X darwin/amd64
In order to build Sentinel HUB you need the source code. Either download the source of a release or clone the Git Repository and make sure it is the latest version.

Clone the GitHub repository: git clone https://github.com/sentinel-official/sentinelhub.git "${HOME}/sentinelhub" Checkout to the latest tag: cd "${HOME}/sentinelhub" commit=$(git rev-list --tags --max-count=1) && \ git checkout $(git describe --tags ${commit}) Build the Binary make install sudo ln -s "${HOME}/sentinelhub" /usr/local/bin/sentinelhub

To download Sentinel HUB go to the Official Repository and download the last source code (either .tar.gz or .zip) Extract the archive: tar xvzf sentinelhub-X.X.X.tar.gz Build the binary cd sentinelhub-X.X.X make install sudo ln -s "${HOME}/sentinelhub" /usr/local/bin/sentinelhub Upon completion of the installation process, you will find a new executable file located at /usr/local/bin/sentinelhub. This file can be launched from your terminal. sentinelhub
The governance commands empower a validator to initiate, cast votes, and contribute deposits to a proposal.
To create a proposal, two methods are available:

Type the following command sentinelhub tx gov submit-proposal <proposal_number> --title="My Proposal" \ --description="My proposal description" \ --type="Text" \ --deposit="<deposit_amount>udvpn" \ --from <validator_key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000 Feel free to customize the title, description, type, deposit amount, and other parameters based on your specific proposal details.

Create the JSON file by using the command sudo nano proposal.json and then input the following content: proposal.json { "title": "My Proposal", "description": "My proposal Description", "type": "Text", "deposit": "<proposal_amount>udvpn" } To create the proposal now type the following command: sentinelhub tx gov submit-proposal \ --proposal="path/to/proposal.json" \ --from <validator_key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000

To initiate a proposal deposit, use the following command: sentinelhub tx gov deposit <proposal_number> \ <deposit_amount>udvpn \ --from <validator_key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000 Make sure to replace <validator_key_name> with the actual validator key name and <proposal_number> with the actual proposal number before executing the command.

To cast your vote on a proposal, use the following command: sentinelhub tx gov vote <proposal_number> \ <yes_or_no> \ --from=<your_keyname> \ --chain-id=sentinelhub-2 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000 Ensure you replace <proposal_number> with the actual proposal number and <yes_or_no> with your vote (either "yes" or "no"). Additionally, specify your key name in place of <your_keyname>.
As you have now built SentinelHub, you can manage your keys.

Open your terminal and type sentinelhub keys add key_name Output - name: key_name type: local address: sent1706klv73nhw2k3p0yl3l88q9p6vlypudrk3nr7 pubkey: '{"@type":"/cosmos.crypto.secp256k1.PubKey","key":"AxU17+KenLYWlmN50t+zDNvOz3YtzrBT6YwzGfi56Wvb"}' mnemonic: "" **Important** write this mnemonic phrase in a safe place. It is the only way to recover your account if you ever forget your password. fee water butter culture rocket focus render asset boost because perfect cargo amused shuffle easily major enact casual sheriff onion screen wall method dizzy The key comes with a "mnemonic phrase", which is serialized into a human-readable 24-word mnemonic. User can recover their associated addresses with the mnemonic phrase. danger It is important that you keep the mnemonic for address secure, as there is no way to recover it. You would not be able to recover and access the funds in the wallet if you forget the mnemonic phrase.

If you already have a seed phrase, use the --recover flag after the command: sentinelhub keys add default_restore --recover You will be prompet to type your mnemonic > Enter your bip39 mnemonic ## Enter your 24-word mnemonic here ##
documents.s: Restore existing key by seed phrase

documents.t: If you already have one or more keys, use the following command to list them: sentinelhub keys list Multiple keys can be created when needed. You can list all keys saved under the storage path. Output - name: default type: local address: sent13zzgfl5n05tk97sq7xdgvx5zmfhx6undyw8722 pubkey: '{"@type":"/cosmos.crypto.secp256k1.PubKey","key":"A6oQhw7UBXp98BxGq8n638dkkYxDhLXHlIsWTdvibY70"}' mnemonic: "" - name: default_recover type: local address: sent1tsefn9fs66gzjzuld0lf402t6p5rhgwcntzahs pubkey: '{"@type":"/cosmos.crypto.secp256k1.PubKey","key":"A0N2NsaJVu4i11jBeoVMvSFDqoGi2nDcJlplMUF9BVS1"}' mnemonic: ""
If you want to view the details of one of your keys, type this command: sentinelhub keys show <key_name> You will get the same output as of the first example where we created the key.

If you want to delete one of your keys, type this command: sentinelhub keys delete <key_name> You will get the following prompt: Key reference will be deleted. Continue? [y/N]: y Key deleted forever (uh oh!) danger Make sure you have backed up the key mnemonic before removing any of your keys, as there will be no way to recover your key without the mnemonic.

If you want to export and backup one of your keys, type the following command: sentinelhub keys export <key_name> You will get the following prompt: Enter passphrase to encrypt the exported key: ## Insert passphrase (must be at least 8 characters)## -----BEGIN TENDERMINT PRIVATE KEY----- kdf: bcrypt salt: ## Salt of the key ## type: secp256k1 imwm2Q8jsWPBg5KfY1Lph5xzEH6UmFE2ovjKTrzST9zePDcuOYdQB7VAhsEP6kMo zWHbcVDvtfxF/sSn8lo1SZWVt+L5UP+BMG1VPAQ= =wSny -----END TENDERMINT PRIVATE KEY-----

Interacting with a node requires a public-private key pair. A keyring is the container that holds these keys, which can be stored in various locations, each with a specified backend type. sentinelhub keys [subcommands] --keyring-backend [backend type]

The default os backend stores the keys in operating system's credential subsystem, which is convenient for most users without compromising on security. Here is a list of password managers corresponding to different operating systems: macOS (since Mac OS 8.6): Keychain Windows: Credentials Management API GNU/Linux: libsecret kwallet

The file backend is the default choice, storing encrypted keys within the application's configuration directory. Each time a user accesses it, such as during container startup, they must enter a password. This interactive requirement prevents running it detached.

The test backend is like a simplified version of the file backend, but without the need for passwords. It keeps keys in plain text within the app's config folder and is meant solely for testing purposes. It's not recommended for production because it's less secure. In this scenario, you can opt to run the container in detached mode instead.

A multisig account is a Sentinel account with a special key requiring more than one signature to approve transactions. This setup enhances account security and enables joint control by multiple parties. To create a multisig account, you must specify: The number of signatures required (threshold). The public keys of all participants. Transactions made with a multisig account need individual signatures from the designated keys. These signatures are then combined into a multisignature. If the number of signatures is below the threshold, the multisignature becomes invalid.
Here’s a step-by-step guide to creating a multisig account named multisig-key using three keys.

Each participant must create their own key. In this example, the keys are named key_1, key_2, and key_3 sentinelhub keys add key_1 Output This is the output details of the key_1​ - name: key_1 type: local address: sent16e34vs3zmp0fjr90rcq888c4padq7g6uh98zk3 pubkey: '{"@type":"/cosmos.crypto.secp256k1.PubKey","key":"A2azxghav4YItrKC0TYXPf2QX2GrDYgOjicNBS5DyPxK"}' mnemonic: "" **Important** write this mnemonic phrase in a safe place. It is the only way to recover your account if you ever forget your password. box yellow pottery flower vendor vivid cigar cream trigger gospel panther twelve donate demise gorilla vacuum grocery theme live kiss proof man follow cheese sentinelhub keys add key_2 Output - name: key_2 type: local address: sent1sd7hd45p5p8ls22a2em9ezly3v3yjr2dm7rqup pubkey: '{"@type":"/cosmos.crypto.secp256k1.PubKey","key":"A6JIWSoDkRnryc+q1Eld8VIJdCTx71Panqa43tgPH45B"}' mnemonic: "" **Important** write this mnemonic phrase in a safe place. It is the only way to recover your account if you ever forget your password. floor tissue frequent fashion shell conduct raw glimpse lonely region pull help little state excuse supreme flight insane hurt empty blanket lecture plug upper sentinelhub keys add key_3 Output - name: key_3 type: local address: sent1r57hfyk2z6txmv7tmuc95erltrw46zfatgnpjt pubkey: '{"@type":"/cosmos.crypto.secp256k1.PubKey","key":"AmFjwqac9h7/gawTExDSbNu5ObNPjxSb9D233gBa64CJ"}' mnemonic: "" **Important** write this mnemonic phrase in a safe place. It is the only way to recover your account if you ever forget your password. detect artefact lemon budget make beyond tape unaware toast mask volume gate crane viable axis utility wheat make home much royal flee depart spawn

After generating the keys, combine their public keys to create the multisig key multisig-key with a 2-of-3 threshold. First, import all the public keys. Use the following commands to add each key: sentinelhub keys add key_1 --pubkey='{"@type":"/cosmos.crypto.secp256k1.PubKey","key":"A2azxghav4YItrKC0TYXPf2QX2GrDYgOjicNBS5DyPxK"}' sentinelhub keys add key_2 --pubkey='{"@type":"/cosmos.crypto.secp256k1.PubKey","key":"A6JIWSoDkRnryc+q1Eld8VIJdCTx71Panqa43tgPH45B"}' sentinelhub keys add key_3 --pubkey='{"@type":"/cosmos.crypto.secp256k1.PubKey","key":"AmFjwqac9h7/gawTExDSbNu5ObNPjxSb9D233gBa64CJ"}' Next, create the multisig key using the following command: sentinelhub keys add --multisig=key_1,key_2,key_3 --multisig-threshold=2 multisig-key Output - name: multisig-key type: multi address: sent13c4medfuu9882c7sqjrt5egqp96l6f4sjd0efh pubkey: '{"@type":"/cosmos.crypto.multisig.LegacyAminoPubKey","threshold":2,"public_keys":[{"@type":"/cosmos.crypto.secp256k1.PubKey","key":"AmFjwqac9h7/gawTExDSbNu5ObNPjxSb9D233gBa64CJ"},{"@type":"/cosmos.crypto.secp256k1.PubKey","key":"A6JIWSoDkRnryc+q1Eld8VIJdCTx71Panqa43tgPH45B"},{"@type":"/cosmos.crypto.secp256k1.PubKey","key":"A2azxghav4YItrKC0TYXPf2QX2GrDYgOjicNBS5DyPxK"}]}' mnemonic: "" The --multisig flag lists the public keys you want to combine. These public keys will create a new multisig public key, which will be stored locally as multisig-key. --multisig-threshold=2 is the minimum number of signatures required to authorize a transaction using the multisig key. By default, the order of keys in the --multisig flag does not matter unless you use the --nosort flag. For example, the following two commands will generate the same multisig key: sentinelhub keys add --multisig=key_1,key_2,key_3 --multisig-threshold=2 multisig-key sentinelhub keys add --multisig=key_1,key_2,key_3 --multisig-threshold=2 multisig-key Fund the Multisig Accoun Before creating transactions, ensure the multisig account has sufficient P2P Coins.

We want to send 5 P2P from our multisig account to sent1nygcr5p33plzq4akfxnl3nr7nf59gnshvtkzs6. To do this, we'll create an offline transaction called unsigned.json, which contains the unsigned transaction in JSON format. This file will then be shared with each signer, who will add their signature and return it to the transaction creator. sentinelhub tx bank send sent13c4medfuu9882c7sqjrt5egqp96l6f4sjd0efh \ sent1nygcr5p33plzq4akfxnl3nr7nf59gnshvtkzs6 \ 5000000udvpn \ --chain-id=sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=500000 \ --generate-only \ --offline \ --account-number=1052698 \ --sequence=0 \ > unsigned.json unsigned.json { "body":{ "messages":[ { "@type":"/cosmos.bank.v1beta1.MsgSend", "from_address":"sent13c4medfuu9882c7sqjrt5egqp96l6f4sjd0efh", "to_address":"sent1nygcr5p33plzq4akfxnl3nr7nf59gnshvtkzs6", "amount":[ { "denom":"udvpn", "amount":"5000000" } ] } ], "memo":"", "timeout_height":"0", "extension_options":[ ], "non_critical_extension_options":[ ] }, "auth_info":{ "signer_infos":[ ], "fee":{ "amount":[ { "denom":"udvpn", "amount":"250000" } ], "gas_limit":"500000", "payer":"", "granter":"" } }, "signatures":[ ] }

The multisig transaction requires signatures from any two of the three key holders. In this example, the keys key_1 and key_3 will be used to sign the transaction. sentinelhub tx sign \ unsigned.json \ --multisig=multisig-key \ --from=key_1 \ --output-document=key_1-signed.json \ --chain-id=sentinelhub-2 \ --node 'https://rpc.sentineldao.com:443' key_1-signed.json { "signatures": [ { "public_key": { "@type": "/cosmos.crypto.secp256k1.PubKey", "key": "A2azxghav4YItrKC0TYXPf2QX2GrDYgOjicNBS5DyPxK" }, "data": { "single": { "mode": "SIGN_MODE_LEGACY_AMINO_JSON", "signature": "/vD4D3/an4JLGUr9LI6G6zWv+AIVZsGLohq3eiHhrVZGJxs1M5fznPX/ABYQpvZ5mmP2OjO0TiiCxO2o05o+Ng==" } }, "sequence": "0" } ] } sentinelhub tx sign \ unsigned.json \ --multisig=multisig-key \ --from=key_3 \ --output-document=key_3-signed.json \ --chain-id=sentinelhub-2 \ --node 'https://rpc.sentineldao.com:443' key_3-signed.json { "signatures": [ { "public_key": { "@type": "/cosmos.crypto.secp256k1.PubKey", "key": "AmFjwqac9h7/gawTExDSbNu5ObNPjxSb9D233gBa64CJ" }, "data": { "single": { "mode": "SIGN_MODE_LEGACY_AMINO_JSON", "signature": "vfBZC78eDgnDV8euRDXRpYvf9SY9q0K6bQw5iHsmbV5ZfarEWdcF7ZNP4Ha0hwnjuLmJzy3rRKLRqjQkUTCyuA==" } }, "sequence": "0" } ] }

Once you have the required signatures, combine them into a single signed transaction. This step finalizes the multisig transaction sentinelhub tx multisign \ unsigned.json \ multisig-key \ key_1-signed.json \ key_3-signed.json \ --output-document=signed.json \ --chain-id=sentinelhub-2 \ --node 'https://rpc.sentineldao.com:443' \ > signed.json signed.json { "body": { "messages": [ { "@type": "/cosmos.bank.v1beta1.MsgSend", "from_address": "sent13c4medfuu9882c7sqjrt5egqp96l6f4sjd0efh", "to_address": "sent1nygcr5p33plzq4akfxnl3nr7nf59gnshvtkzs6", "amount": [ { "denom": "udvpn", "amount": "5000000" } ] } ], "memo": "", "timeout_height": "0", "extension_options": [], "non_critical_extension_options": [] }, "auth_info": { "signer_infos": [ { "public_key": { "@type": "/cosmos.crypto.multisig.LegacyAminoPubKey", "threshold": 2, "public_keys": [ { "@type": "/cosmos.crypto.secp256k1.PubKey", "key": "AmFjwqac9h7/gawTExDSbNu5ObNPjxSb9D233gBa64CJ" }, { "@type": "/cosmos.crypto.secp256k1.PubKey", "key": "A6JIWSoDkRnryc+q1Eld8VIJdCTx71Panqa43tgPH45B" }, { "@type": "/cosmos.crypto.secp256k1.PubKey", "key": "A2azxghav4YItrKC0TYXPf2QX2GrDYgOjicNBS5DyPxK" } ] }, "mode_info": { "multi": { "bitarray": { "extra_bits_stored": 3, "elems": "oA==" }, "mode_infos": [ { "single": { "mode": "SIGN_MODE_LEGACY_AMINO_JSON" } }, { "single": { "mode": "SIGN_MODE_LEGACY_AMINO_JSON" } } ] } }, "sequence": "0" } ], "fee": { "amount": [ { "denom": "udvpn", "amount": "250000" } ], "gas_limit": "500000", "payer": "", "granter": "" } }, "signatures": [ "CkC98FkLvx4OCcNXx65ENdGli9/1Jj2rQrptDDmIeyZtXll9qsRZ1wXtk0/gdrSHCeO4uYnPLetEotGqNCRRMLK4CkD+8PgPf9qfgksZSv0sjobrNa/4AhVmwYuiGrd6IeGtVkYnGzUzl/Oc9f8AFhCm9nmaY/Y6M7ROKILE7ajTmj42" ] }

Finally, broadcast the signed transaction to the blockchain network. sentinelhub tx broadcast \ signed.json \ --node 'https://rpc.sentineldao.com:443' Output code: 0 codespace: "" data: "" events: [] gas_used: "0" gas_wanted: "0" height: "0" info: "" logs: [] raw_log: '[]' timestamp: "" tx: null txhash: 5308DBB812FE3D7AC308C6B75044D3BCB085A9F72FC4FFE258421940E9842953
This section describes the commands available from sentinelhub, the command line interface that connects a running sentinelhub process.

Add a genesis account to genesis.json. The provided account must specify the account address or key name and a list of initial coins. If a key name is given, the address will be looked up in the local Keybase. The list of initial tokens must contain valid denominations. Accounts may optionally be supplied with vesting parameters. Syntax sentinelhub add-genesis-account [address_or_key_name] [coin][,[coin]] [flags]
Collects genesis transactions and outputs them to genesis.json. Syntax sentinelhub collect-gentxs [flags]

Create or query an application CLI configuration file sentinelhub config <key> [value] [flags] Output This is the output of sentinelhub config​ { "chain-id": "", "keyring-backend": "os", "output": "text", "node": "tcp://localhost:26657", "broadcast-mode": "sync" }

Tool for helping with debugging your application. Syntax sentinelhub debug [flags] sentinelhub debug [subcommand] Available subcommands This is the output of sentinelhub debug​ addr Convert an address between hex and bech32 pubkey Decode a pubkey from proto JSON raw-bytes Convert raw bytes output (eg. [10 21 13 255]) to hex
Exports the state to JSON. Syntax sentinelhub export [flags]

Generate a genesis transaction that creates a validator with a self-delegation, that is signed by the key in the Keyring referenced by a given name. A node ID and Bech32 consensus pubkey may optionally be provided. If they are omitted, they will be retrieved from the priv_validator.json file. The following default parameters are included: delegation amount: 100000000stake commission rate: 0.1 commission max rate: 0.2 commission max change rate: 0.01 minimum self delegation: 1 Syntax sentinelhub gentx [key_name] [amount][denom] [flags] Example sentinelhub gentx my-key-name 1000000udvpn --home=/path/to/home/dir --keyring-backend=os --chain-id=sentinelhub-2 \ --moniker="myValidator" \ --commission-max-change-rate=0.01 \ --commission-max-rate=1.0 \ --commission-rate=0.07 \ --details="..." \ --security-contact="..." \ --website="..."
Help provides help for any command in the application. Simply type sentinelhub help [path to command] for full details. Syntax sentinelhub help [command] [flags]
Initialize validators's and node's configuration files Syntax sentinelhub init [moniker] [flags] Example sentinelhub init my-node

Keyring management commands. These keys may be in any format supported by the Tendermint crypto library and can be used by light-clients, full nodes, or any other application that needs to sign with a private key. The keyring supports the following backends: os Uses the operating system's default credentials store. file Uses encrypted file-based keystore within the app's configuration directory. This keyring will request a password each time it is accessed, which may occur multiple times in a single command resulting in repeated password prompts. kwallet Uses KDE Wallet Manager as a credentials management application. pass Uses the pass command line utility to store and retrieve keys. test Stores keys insecurely to disk. It does not prompt for a password to be unlocked and it should be use only for testing purposes. kwallet and pass backends depend on external tools. Refer to their respective documentation for more information: KWallet https://github.com/KDE/kwallet pass https://www.passwordstore.org/ The pass backend requires GnuPG: https://gnupg.org/ Syntax sentinelhub keys [command] Available subcommands This is the output of sentinelhub keys​ add Add an encrypted private key (either newly generated or recovered), encrypt it, and save to <name> file delete Delete the given keys export Export private keys import Import private keys into the local keybase import-hex Import private keys into the local keybase list List all keys list-key-types List all key types migrate Migrate keys from amino to proto serialization format mnemonic Compute the bip39 mnemonic for some input entropy parse Parse address from hex to bech32 and vice versa rename Rename an existing key show Retrieve key information by name or address tip For more detailed usage instructions for keys, please refer to the related section here

Manages queries. Syntax sentinelhub query [flags] sentinelhub query [subcommand] Available subcommands This is the output of sentinelhub query​ account Query for account by address auth Querying commands for the auth module authz Querying commands for the authz module bank Querying commands for the bank module block Get verified data for the block at given height distribution Querying commands for the distribution module evidence Query for evidence by hash or for all (paginated) submitted evidence feegrant Querying commands for the feegrant module gov Querying commands for the governance module group Querying commands for the group module ibc Querying commands for the IBC module ibc-fee IBC relayer incentivization query subcommands ibc-transfer IBC fungible token transfer query subcommands interchain-accounts IBC interchain accounts query subcommands mint Querying commands for the minting module nft Querying commands for the nft module oracle Querying commands for the Oracle module params Querying commands for the params module slashing Querying commands for the slashing module staking Querying commands for the staking module swap Querying commands for the swap module tendermint-validator-set Get the full tendermint validator set at given height tx Query for a transaction by hash txs Query for paginated transactions that match a set of events upgrade Querying commands for the upgrade module vpn Querying commands for the VPN module wasm Querying commands for the wasm module

A state rollback is performed to recover from an incorrect application state transition, when Tendermint has persisted an incorrect app hash and is thus unable to make progress. Rollback overwrites a state at height n with the state at height n - 1. The application also roll back to height n - 1. No blocks are removed, so upon restarting Tendermint the transactions in block n will be re-executed against the application. Syntax sentinelhub rollback [flags]

Run the full node application with Tendermint in or out of process. By default, the application will run with Tendermint in process. Pruning options can be provided via the '--pruning' flag or alternatively with '--pruning-keep-recent', 'pruning-keep-every', and 'pruning-interval' together. For '--pruning' the options are as follows: default: the last 100 states are kept in addition to every 500th state; pruning at 10 block intervals nothing: all historic states will be saved, nothing will be deleted (i.e. archiving node) everything: all saved states will be deleted, storing only the current and previous state; pruning at 10 block intervals custom: allow pruning options to be manually specified through 'pruning-keep-recent', 'pruning-keep-every', and 'pruning-interval' Node halting configurations exist in the form of two flags: '--halt-height' and '--halt-time'. During the ABCI Commit phase, the node will check if the current block height is greater than or equal to the halt-height or if the current block time is greater than or equal to the halt-time. If so, the node will attempt to gracefully shutdown and the block will not be committed. In addition, the node will not be able to commit subsequent blocks. For profiling and benchmarking purposes, CPU profiling can be enabled via the '--cpu-profile' flag which accepts a path for the resulting pprof file. The node may be started in a 'query only' mode where only the gRPC and JSON HTTP API services are enabled via the 'grpc-only' flag. In this mode, Tendermint is bypassed and can be used when legacy queries are needed after an on-chain upgrade is performed. Note, when enabled, gRPC will also be automatically enabled. Syntax sentinelhub start [flags]

Displays the status of a remote node (default "tcp://localhost:26657"). Syntax sentinelhub status [flags] Output This is the output of sentinelhub status​ { "NodeInfo":{ "protocol_version":{ "p2p":"8", "block":"11", "app":"0" }, "id":"fd1c929dc0c2ce6418b6ed31747469de6c7b15bb", "listen_addr":"tcp://0.0.0.0:26656", "network":"sentinelhub-2", "version":"0.34.27", "channels":"40202122233038606100", "moniker":"2-private-node", "other":{ "tx_index":"on", "rpc_address":"tcp://0.0.0.0:26657" } }, "SyncInfo":{ "latest_block_hash":"64012F64E1BD3CDF52E8A68EE4CB8BA42740C7550704800536109DF8C6F24E9A", "latest_app_hash":"B9648EC2A213E81D9FE42932F69113FA9F0965FA3DD0C4E4D15DDB7940DC0C8F", "latest_block_height":"12638588", "latest_block_time":"2023-09-10T02:09:42.963271871Z", "earliest_block_hash":"11E60037E22F6ABDF29DE851063E4C0E0A34E4D3D067EDA55B1674A0257E7D03", "earliest_app_hash":"E3B0C44298FC1C149AFBF4C8996FB92427AE41E4649B934CA495991B7852B855", "earliest_block_height":"901801", "earliest_block_time":"2021-05-29T14:30:00Z", "catching_up":false }, "ValidatorInfo":{ "Address":"6D2F88F51486E74768A85DA4E375F3551F2762A8", "PubKey":{ "type":"tendermint/PubKeyEd25519", "value":"S+wi725X8wyDhgEmRlR0xnjuxBDntlBGsLLMmpIFXiY=" }, "VotingPower":"0" } }

Manages the Tendermint protocol. Syntax sentinelhub tendermint [command] [flags] Available subcommands This is the output of sentinelhub tendermint​ reset-state Remove all the data and WAL show-address Shows this node's tendermint validator consensus address show-node-id Show this node's ID show-validator Show this node's tendermint validator info unsafe-reset-all (unsafe) Remove all the data and WAL, reset this node's validator to genesis state version Print tendermint libraries' version

Retrieves a transaction by its hash, account sequence, or signature. Syntax sentinelhub tx [flags] sentinelhub tx [subcommand] Available subcommands This is the output of sentinelhub tx​ authz Authorization transactions subcommands bank Bank transaction subcommands broadcast Broadcast transactions generated offline crisis Crisis transactions subcommands decode Decode a binary encoded transaction string distribution Distribution transactions subcommands encode Encode transactions generated offline evidence Evidence transaction subcommands feegrant Feegrant transactions subcommands gov Governance transactions subcommands group Group transaction subcommands ibc IBC transaction subcommands ibc-fee IBC relayer incentivization transaction subcommands ibc-transfer IBC fungible token transfer transaction subcommands interchain-accounts IBC interchain accounts transaction subcommands multi-sign Generate multisig signatures for transactions generated offline multisign-batch Assemble multisig transactions in batch from batch signatures nft nft transactions subcommands sign Sign a transaction generated offline sign-batch Sign transaction batch files slashing Slashing transaction subcommands staking Staking transaction subcommands swap Swap module sub-commands validate-signatures validate transactions signatures vesting Vesting transaction subcommands vpn VPN transactions subcommands wasm Wasm transaction subcommands
validates the genesis file at the default location or at the location passed as an argument. Syntax sentinelhub validate-genesis [file] [flags] Example sentinelhub validate-genesis genesis.json
Print the application binary version information. Syntax sentinelhub version [flags]
The account module is dedicated to essential account details, including the account number, sequence, and public key.

To query an account, use the following command: sentinelhub query account \ <account_address> \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 Example Output Growth DAO Address '@type': /cosmos.auth.v1beta1.BaseAccount account_number: "52632" address: sent1nygcr5p33plzq4akfxnl3nr7nf59gnshvtkzs6 pub_key: '@type': /cosmos.crypto.secp256k1.PubKey key: A4r6ULL86mKsQxECNkP+meRPbUuP2dR6qtHgD9Ma4NX2 sequence: "324"
Querying commands for the auth module.

Retrieve all the accounts sentinelhub query auth accounts \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 Example Output accounts: - '@type': /cosmos.auth.v1beta1.BaseAccount account_number: "290737" address: sent1llllth4ntelpjk59zxdksl2tdj6t7w8tglr97y pub_key: null sequence: "0" - '@type': /cosmos.auth.v1beta1.BaseAccount account_number: "161577" address: sent1lll7cyvcnc5cldmlapwwpcvj2atnxjg27lkx9c pub_key: null sequence: "0" pagination: next_key: //+1x/RHu6glTRiZ8/F17KBnYr0= total: "0"

Retrieve a specific account. sentinelhub query auth account [account_address] \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 Example Output '@type': /cosmos.auth.v1beta1.BaseAccount account_number: "290737" address: sent1llllth4ntelpjk59zxdksl2tdj6t7w8tglr97y pub_key: null sequence: "0"

Retrieve module account info by module name. sentinelhub query auth module-account [module_name] \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 Example Output account: '@type': /cosmos.auth.v1beta1.ModuleAccount base_account: account_number: "588024" address: sent1xds4f0m87ajl3a6az6s2enhxrd0wta48ta2nhs pub_key: null sequence: "0" name: wasm permissions: - burner

Retrieve the current auth parameters. sentinelhub query auth params \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 Example Output max_memo_characters: "256" sig_verify_cost_ed25519: "590" sig_verify_cost_secp256k1: "1000" tx_sig_limit: "7" tx_size_cost_per_byte: "150"
Querying commands for the authz module.

The query distribution module focuses on managing account balances and monitoring the coin supply.

To query an account balance, use the following command: sentinelhub query bank balances \ <account_address> \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 Example Output Growth DAO Address balances: - amount: "12002" denom: ibc/31FEE1A2A9F9C01113F90BD0BBCCE8FD6BBB8585FAF109A2101827DD1D5B95B8 - amount: "339645" denom: ibc/B1C0DDB14F25279A2026BC8794E12B259F8BDA546A3C5132CCAEE4431CE36783 - amount: "1301" denom: ibc/ED07A3391A112B175915CD8FAF43A2DA8E4790EDE12566649D0C2F97716B8518 - amount: "12660890169349" denom: udvpn pagination: next_key: null total: "0"

documents.t: The query distribution module encompasses aspects such as community pool management, validator commissions, delegator rewards, parameter settings, and slashing mechanisms.

Querying commands for the feegrant module, which allows one account to grant fee allowances to another.
Query details of a single fee grant between a granter and grantee. sentinelhub query feegrant grant <granter_address> <grantee_address> \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443
Query all fee grants received by a grantee. sentinelhub query feegrant grants-by-grantee <grantee_address> \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443
Query all fee grants issued by a granter. sentinelhub query feegrant grants-by-granter <granter_address> \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443
The governance module queries proposals on the blockchain.

Given the recent performance of Sentinel, marked by a significant number of products either already on the market or poised for imminent release, it is an opportune moment to establish a marketing fund. This fund will be dedicated to financing paid advertising across a diverse range of platforms. Our strategy includes leveraging Telegram groups, sponsored Telegram ads, Twitter (X), LinkedIn, and any other social platforms that are deemed effective. The primary goal of this initiative is to maximize our reach, encouraging a greater number of users to download Sentinel-based VPNs. To finance this initiative, we plan to gradually convert P2P coins into USDT. This process will be carefully managed to minimize market impact. We will explore two primary avenues for this conversion: engaging in over-the-counter (OTC) transactions with individual parties or executing measured sales on exchanges. In the case of exchange sales, we propose a cautious approach, such as selling around $100 per day, to avoid any adverse effects on the coin's price. This strategy ensures a steady funding stream By voting NO, you disagree with the proposal. By voting ABSTAIN, you refrain from voting. Querying commands for the wasm module (CosmWasm), which handles smart contracts on the Sentinel chain.
Print out metadata of a code ID. sentinelhub query wasm code-info <code_id> \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443
Download wasm bytecode for a given code ID. sentinelhub query wasm code <code_id> <output_file> \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443
List all wasm bytecode on the chain. sentinelhub query wasm list-code \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443
Print out metadata of a contract given its address. sentinelhub query wasm contract <contract_address> \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443
Print out the code history for a contract given its address. sentinelhub query wasm contract-history <contract_address> \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443
Query the state of a wasm contract. sentinelhub query wasm contract-state smart <contract_address> <query_json> \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443
List all wasm contracts instantiated from a given code ID. sentinelhub query wasm list-contract-by-code <code_id> \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443
List all contracts created by a specific address. sentinelhub query wasm list-contracts-by-creator <creator_address> \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443
List all pinned code IDs. sentinelhub query wasm pinned \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443
Query the current wasm parameters. sentinelhub query wasm params \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443
Build a contract address from the given code hash and creator info. sentinelhub query wasm build-address <code_hash> <creator_address> [salt] \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443
Get the libwasmvm version. sentinelhub query wasm libwasmvm-version
Authorize and revoke access to execute transactions on behalf of your address

Grant permission for one address to spend on behalf of another address. sentinelhub tx authz grant \ <grantee_address> \ send \ --from <granter_key_name> \ --spend-limit <amount>udvpn \ --expiration 1730799045 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000

Revoke permission for one address to spend on behalf of another address. sentinelhub tx authz revoke \ <grantee_address> \ /cosmos.bank.v1beta1.MsgSend \ --from <granter_key_name> \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000

To initiate the transaction on behalf of the granter account, follow these steps: The granter must first generate an offline transaction using the following command which prepares the transaction details and saves them in the tx.json file. sentinelhub tx bank send \ <granter_address> \ <recipient_address> \ <amount>udvpn \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --generate-only > tx.json The grantee is then responsible for broadcasting the transaction. Ensure that the grantee has sufficient fees to cover the transaction costs. Use the following command: sentinelhub tx authz exec tx.json \ --from <grantee_key_name> \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000

Authorize an address to cast votes on behalf of another address for proposals. sentinelhub tx authz grant \ <grantee_address> \ generic \ --msg-type /cosmos.gov.v1beta1.MsgVote \ --from <granter_key_name> \ --expiration 1730799045 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000 Some notes on the flags: the expiration is set to default at 1730799045 which is 1 year

Revoke authorization for an address to cast votes on behalf of another address for proposals. sentinelhub tx authz revoke \ <grantee_address> \ /cosmos.gov.v1beta1.MsgVote \ --from <granter_key_name> \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000

Grant authorization for one address to withdraw staking rewards on behalf of another address. sentinelhub tx authz grant \ <grantee_address> \ generic \ --msg-type /cosmos.distribution.v1beta1.MsgSetWithdrawAddress \ --from <granter_key_name> \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 \ --expiration 1730799045 \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000

Revoke the authorization for one address to withdraw staking rewards on behalf of another address. sentinelhub tx authz revoke \ <grantee_address> \ /cosmos.distribution.v1beta1.MsgSetWithdrawAddress \ --from <granter_key_name> \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000

Authorize one specific address to claim validator commissions on behalf of the validator's address. sentinelhub tx authz grant \ <grantee_address> \ generic \ --msg-type /cosmos.distribution.v1beta1.MsgWithdrawValidatorCommission \ --from <granter_key_name> \ --expiration 1730799045 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000

Revoke the authorization for claiming validator rewards on behalf of the validator's address for a specific account. sentinelhub tx authz revoke \ <grantee_address> \ /cosmos.distribution.v1beta1.MsgWithdrawValidatorCommission \ --from <granter_key_name> \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000
Transaction commands for the distribution module, which manages staking rewards, commission withdrawals, and the community pool.

Withdraw rewards from a given delegation address. Optionally withdraw validator commission with the --commission flag. sentinelhub tx distribution withdraw-rewards <sentvaloper_address> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 To also withdraw validator commission: sentinelhub tx distribution withdraw-rewards <sentvaloper_address> \ --commission \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Withdraw all delegation rewards for a delegator. sentinelhub tx distribution withdraw-all-rewards \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Change the default withdraw address for rewards associated with your account. sentinelhub tx distribution set-withdraw-addr <withdrawal_address> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Fund the community pool with the specified amount. sentinelhub tx distribution fund-community-pool \ <amount>udvpn \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443
Transaction commands for the feegrant module, which allows one account to grant fee allowances to another. This is useful for dVPN applications that want to sponsor transaction fees for their users.

Grant a fee allowance to an address, allowing them to use the granter's funds for transaction fees. sentinelhub tx feegrant grant \ <granter_address> \ <grantee_address> \ --spend-limit <amount>udvpn \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 You can also set an expiration with the --expiration flag (RFC 3339 timestamp).

Revoke an existing fee grant from a grantee. sentinelhub tx feegrant revoke \ <granter_address> \ <grantee_address> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

To broadcast the transaction that has been generated and signed offline, use the following command: sentinelhub tx broadcast \ signed.json \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 If you wish to engage in additional offline transactions, such as delegating, claiming rewards, unbonding, etc., you simply need to include the following four fields, as demonstrated in the process of creating and signing an offline transaction: --generate-only \ --offline \ --account-number=<account_number> \ --sequence=<sequence_number> \ > unsigned.json To sign the transaction, use the sign command as previously shown, specifying the following fields: --offline \ --account-number=<account_number> \ --sequence=<sequence_number>

To initiate an offline transaction using your terminal, follow these steps: sentinelhub tx bank send \ <sender_address> \ <recipient_address> \ <amount>udvpn \ --chain-id=sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000 \ --generate-only \ --account-number=<account_number> \ --sequence=<sequence_number> \ > unsigned.json In comparison to online transactions, there are additional fields that require clarification: --generate-only: This option generates the transaction without executing it. --account-number: Refers to the account number associated with your wallet. --sequence: It represents the transaction number associated with the address up to that point. > unsigned.json: This command directs the output to a file named unsigned.json. After running this command, an unsigned.json file will be created. Keep in mind that this file must be signed offline before proceeding to broadcast the transaction.

To sign an offline transaction using your terminal, follow these steps: sentinelhub tx sign \ unsigned.json \ --from=<your_keyname> \ --output-document=signed.json \ --chain-id=sentinelhub-2 \ --offline \ --account-number=<account_number> \ --sequence=<sequence_number> In comparison to online transactions, there are additional fields that require clarification: --output-document: This command directs the output to a file named signed.json. --offline: This flag explicitly indicates that the transaction is intended to be conducted offline. --account-number: Refers to the account number associated with your wallet --sequence: It represents the transaction number associated with the address up to that point. After running this command, an signed.json file will be created. Keep in mind that broadcasting this file to the network is essential for the execution of the transaction.

To send a transaction to another sentinel address type on your terminal sentinelhub tx bank send \ <sender_address> \ <recipient_address> \ <amout>udvpn \ --chain-id=sentinelhub-2 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000 Ensure to replace <sender_address>, <recipient_address>, and <amount> with the appropriate values for your transaction. Adjust the gas prices and limit as needed for the specific requirements of your transaction.
With Sentinel Hub, you can execute various operations to engage with staking.

To delegate to another validator address type the following command in your terminal: sentinelhub tx staking delegate <sentvaloper_validator_address> \ <amount>udvpn \ --from=<your_keyname> \ --chain-id=sentinelhub-2 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000 Make sure to replace <sentvaloper_validator_address>, <amount>, and <your_keyname> with the appropriate values for your delegation.

To redelegate to another validator address type the following command in your terminal: sentinelhub tx staking redelegate \ <source_validator_address> \ <destination_validator_address> \ <amount>udvpn \ --from=<your_keyname> \ --chain-id=sentinelhub-2 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000 Make sure to replace <source_validator_address>, <destination_validator_address>, <amount>, and <your_keyname> with the appropriate values for your delegation.

To unbond your staked amount from a validator type on your terminal sentinelhub tx staking unbond <sentvaloper_validator_address> \ <amount>udvpn \ --from=<delegator_address> \ --chain-id=sentinelhub-2 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000 This command will unbond the specified <amount> of udvpn tokens from the validator identified by <sentvaloper_validator_address>. Ensure that you replace <your_keyname> with the actual name of your key.

To claim both your staking rewards and commissions, execute the following command in your terminal: sentinelhub tx distribution withdraw-rewards <sentvaloper_validator_address> \ --from=<your_keyname> \ --commission \ --chain-id=sentinelhub-2 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000 Replace <sentvaloper_validator_address> with the actual validator address you staked with, and <your_keyname> with the name of your key. Adjust the gas prices and limit according to your preference and network conditions.

To set an alternative address for withdrawing your rewards, use the following command: sentinelhub tx distribution set-withdraw-addr <withdrawal_address> \ --from=<your_keyname> \ --chain-id=sentinelhub-2 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000 Make sure to replace <withdrawal_address> with the actual address you want to set as your withdrawal destination and <your_keyname> with your specific key name. Adjust other parameters as needed.

Create a new validator and initialize it with a self-delegation. sentinelhub tx staking create-validator \ --broadcast-mode=block \ --min-self-delegation=1 \ --amount=<self_delegation_amount>udvpn \ --commission-max-change-rate=0.01 \ --commission-max-rate=0.2 \ --commission-rate=0.07 \ --moniker="<validator_name>" \ --pubkey="<full_node_public_key>" \ --from="<validator_key_name>" \ --chain-id=sentinelhub-2 \ --gas=300000 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn If you're currently in the validator creation process, refer to this page in the full node guide for further assistance.

The Edit-Validator transaction lets you update different aspects of your validator, like the description, website, security contact, commissions, PGP identity, and moniker. sentinelhub tx staking edit-validator \ --identity=<your_pgp_key_with_no_spaces> \ --website="<https://your_new_website.com>" \ --security-contact="<email_address>" \ --details="<new_validator_description>" --moniker="<new_validator_moniker>" \ --commission-rate=<new_commission_rate> \ --from="<validator_key_name>" \ --chain-id=sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices=0.5udvpn \ --gas=300000 If you want to update your validator's commission-rate, ensure the new value falls within the limits set by the commission-max-change-rate and commission-max-rate parameters defined when the validator was created. Please note that in this scenario, the flag --node is not utilized, assuming you are executing this command directly from your validator machine.

The Unjail Validator transaction allows you to release your validator from a jailed state and restore it to its usual operational status. sentinelhub tx slashing unjail \ --from="<validator_key_name>" \ --chain-id=sentinelhub-2
Commands for interacting with the Sentinel VPN modules: providers, plans, nodes, subscriptions, sessions, and leases.

Register a new provider with a name and optional details. sentinelhub tx vpn provider register-provider \ <provider_name> \ --description "<provider_description>" \ --identity "<provider_identity>" \ --website "https://example.com" \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Update the details of an existing provider. sentinelhub tx vpn provider update-provider-details \ --description "<new_description>" \ --identity "<new_identity>" \ --website "https://new-website.com" \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Update the operational status of an existing provider. sentinelhub tx vpn provider update-provider-status \ <active|inactive> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Create a new subscription plan with bytes, duration, pricing details, and privacy setting. sentinelhub tx vpn plan create-plan \ <bytes> \ <duration> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Update the details of an existing subscription plan. sentinelhub tx vpn plan update-plan-details \ <plan_id> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Activate or deactivate a subscription plan. sentinelhub tx vpn plan update-plan-status \ <plan_id> <active|inactive> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Link a community-hosted node to a subscription plan. sentinelhub tx vpn plan link-node \ <plan_id> \ <sentnode_address> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

documents.t: Remove a node from a subscription plan. sentinelhub tx vpn plan unlink-node \ <plan_id> \ <sentnode_address> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443
documents.s: Unlink a Node from a Plan

documents.t: Register a new node with remote addresses and pricing details. sentinelhub tx vpn node register-node \ <remote_addrs> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Update the pricing and remote URL details of an existing node. sentinelhub tx vpn node update-node-details \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Update the operational status of a node. sentinelhub tx vpn node update-node-status \ <active|inactive> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Start a session directly with a node. sentinelhub tx vpn node start-session \ <sentnode_address> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

documents.t: Start a subscription for a plan. sentinelhub tx vpn subscription start-subscription \ <plan_id> \ --denom udvpn \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Renew an existing subscription. sentinelhub tx vpn subscription renew-subscription \ <subscription_id> \ --denom udvpn \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Cancel an active subscription. sentinelhub tx vpn subscription cancel-subscription \ <subscription_id> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Update the details of an existing subscription. sentinelhub tx vpn subscription update-subscription \ <subscription_id> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Share a subscription with another account by allocating bytes. sentinelhub tx vpn subscription share-subscription \ <subscription_id> \ <account_address> \ <bytes> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Start a session for a subscription and node. sentinelhub tx vpn subscription start-session \ <subscription_id> \ <sentnode_address> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Update the details of an existing session (download bytes, upload bytes, duration). sentinelhub tx vpn session update-session \ <session_id> <download_bytes> <upload_bytes> <duration> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Start a lease with a node for the specified duration. sentinelhub tx vpn lease start-lease \ <sentnode_address> \ <hours> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Renew an existing lease for a specified duration. sentinelhub tx vpn lease renew-lease \ <lease_id> \ <hours> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443

Update the details of an existing lease. sentinelhub tx vpn lease update-lease \ <lease_id> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443
End an existing lease. sentinelhub tx vpn lease end-lease \ <lease_id> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443
Transaction commands for the swap module, which allows swapping SENT tokens to DVPN.

Swap coins from SENT to DVPN by providing the original transaction hash, receiver address, and amount. sentinelhub tx swap swap \ <tx_hash> \ <receiver_address> \ <amount> \ --from <key_name> \ --chain-id sentinelhub-2 \ --gas-prices 0.5udvpn \ --gas 300000 \ --node https://rpc.sentinel.co:443 Replace <tx_hash> with the SENT transaction hash, <receiver_address> with the destination address, and <amount> with the amount to swap.

The Sentinel dVPN protocol runs on Solana. Its on-chain logic is the dvpn Anchor program, which manages nodes, providers, plans, subscriptions, leases, channels, grants, and payments. note Pages in other sections, including dVPN Nodes and dVPN CLI, describe the earlier Sentinel Hub (Cosmos) flow. For the Solana flow, use the pages in this section.
Node Operators: run a dVPN node and manage it on-chain. Clients: connect to nodes with the sentinel-dvpn CLI and a client daemon. dVPN Program: the program's accounts and instructions.

Binary Role sentinel-dvpn Command-line tool for wallets, on-chain actions, and client sessions. sentinel-dvpnd Daemon. Runs a node, provider, or client instance. The instance tag sets the role: n<N> for node, p<N> for provider, c<N> for client.

Everything in this section is built from the sentinel-solana monorepo: Folder Contents sentinel-dvpn The sentinel-dvpn CLI. sentinel-dvpnd The sentinel-dvpnd daemon. sentinel-go-sdk Go SDK: VPN protocol integrations (WireGuard, AmneziaWG, OpenVPN, V2Ray, Xray, Hysteria2), node and provider APIs, and the on-chain program client. sentinel-programs The dvpn and distributor Anchor programs, their IDLs, and the generated Go client. sentinel-snapshot Chain snapshot tooling. The CLI and daemon need Go 1.27.3. The programs also need Rust 1.97.1, Anchor 1.2.2, and Solana (Agave) 4.3.2.

These docs target devnet: Item Devnet value dVPN program ID J52dyXW3a6mkatvrQct3fo6dA9vqUtcsdBt5gGqrTBXs dVPN token mint (Token-2022) Hen2LVP6KooGaXEvdSyCHWghsEY4gLLn7wix8z6zHFSa RPC https://api.devnet.solana.com (the default for devnet builds) To get devnet SOL for fees, use the official Solana faucet. The source of devnet dVPN tokens is TBD.

Connect to a Sentinel dVPN node with the sentinel-dvpn CLI and a client daemon. Payments are on Solana. Draft These pages come from the sentinel-dvpn and sentinel-dvpnd source in sentinel-solana and the binaries' --help output. The commands have not yet been run end to end on devnet. The source of devnet dVPN tokens is TBD.

The sentinel-dvpn CLI and the sentinel-dvpnd daemon, built for devnet with the program ID and mint set. See Build the binaries. A plain go build leaves them unset, and every chain call fails. An owner wallet with SOL for fees and dVPN tokens for payment. On devnet, get SOL from the official Solana faucet. A client daemon with its own SOL balance. The daemon signs channel transactions and pays their fees with its operator key. Its public key is in the init output.

Your owner wallet holds the dVPN tokens and pays for on-chain actions. Your client daemon (sentinel-dvpnd, instance tag c<N>) holds the session keys, signs channel transactions, and talks to nodes. The CLI (sentinel-dvpn) starts and stops sessions through the daemon, with --instance c<N>.

Route Use it when Command New channel You pay a node directly, per GB or per hour, by voucher or stream. client start --instance c0 --node <NODE> --new-channel --mode voucher --escrow-base-units <N> Existing channel You already have a channel with this node. client start --instance c0 --node <NODE> --channel <CHANNEL> Provider ticket You hold a subscription from a provider. client start --instance c0 --node <NODE> --provider <PROVIDER> --subscription <SUB> --ticket Setup, then connection, are in the next two pages: Set up the wallet and client daemon Connect to a node
Before you connect, find a node and check it.

These commands read the chain and don't need --instance: sentinel-dvpn node search --help sentinel-dvpn node show <NODE_ADDRESS> Check a node's signed metadata and health before you pay it: sentinel-dvpn node inspect <NODE_ADDRESS> inspect verifies the node's signed metadata and checks its health over a pinned connection.

Choose the route that matches how you pay. See Ways to pay on the overview page. client commands go through your client daemon, so they need --instance c0. --node is required, and you must pick one of --new-channel, --channel, --ticket, or --ticket-hash. New channel, paid by voucher: sentinel-dvpn client start \ --instance c0 \ --node <NODE_ADDRESS> \ --new-channel \ --mode voucher \ --escrow-base-units <BASE_UNITS> Existing channel: sentinel-dvpn client start --instance c0 --node <NODE_ADDRESS> --channel <CHANNEL_ADDRESS> Provider ticket: sentinel-dvpn client start \ --instance c0 \ --node <NODE_ADDRESS> \ --provider <PROVIDER_ADDRESS> \ --subscription <SUBSCRIPTION_ADDRESS> \ --ticket Use --mode stream for pay-as-you-go streaming instead of vouchers.

sentinel-dvpn client sessions --instance c0 sentinel-dvpn client status <SESSION_ID> --instance c0 sentinel-dvpn client watch <SESSION_ID> --instance c0 sentinel-dvpn client stop <SESSION_ID> --instance c0 client watch streams updates until you stop it. To list your channels and the tickets the daemon holds: sentinel-dvpn client channels --instance c0 sentinel-dvpn client tickets --instance c0

Tickets are access proofs issued by a provider. These commands don't need --instance: sentinel-dvpn ticket request --help sentinel-dvpn ticket show <ENCODED_TICKET> sentinel-dvpn ticket verify <ENCODED_TICKET> ticket verify checks the ticket against the provider's on-chain owner.

Leases rent a node by the hour. These are chain commands, so they don't take --instance. Run --help for the flags: sentinel-dvpn lease open-lease --help sentinel-dvpn lease fund-leases --help sentinel-dvpn lease redeem-lease-vouchers --help sentinel-dvpn lease start-close-lease --help sentinel-dvpn lease close-lease --help Withdraw any unused user balance: sentinel-dvpn user withdraw-user-balance --help Close a subscription when you no longer need it: sentinel-dvpn subscription close-subscription --help

Both binaries come from the sentinel-solana monorepo, in its sentinel-dvpn and sentinel-dvpnd folders. You need Go 1.27.3. Each folder's Makefile bakes in the network, program ID, and mint. Its default network is mainnet, so pass the devnet values explicitly: git clone https://github.com/sentinel-official/sentinel-solana.git cd sentinel-solana for dir in sentinel-dvpn sentinel-dvpnd; do make -C "$dir" build \ SENTINEL_NETWORK=devnet \ SENTINEL_PROGRAM_ID=J52dyXW3a6mkatvrQct3fo6dA9vqUtcsdBt5gGqrTBXs \ SENTINEL_MINT=Hen2LVP6KooGaXEvdSyCHWghsEY4gLLn7wix8z6zHFSa done The outputs are sentinel-dvpn/bin/sentinel-dvpn and sentinel-dvpnd/bin/sentinel-dvpnd. Move them onto your PATH. sentinel-dvpn version should show "network":"devnet".

sentinel-dvpn key new owner sentinel-dvpn key show owner key new encrypts the key by default. Use --unencrypted only on a test machine. The public key from key show is the owner wallet address. Pass it as --owner to the daemon below.

Your wallet needs SOL for fees before any of the next commands work. On devnet, request it from the official Solana faucet. Devnet builds default to https://api.devnet.solana.com. To use another endpoint, create the CLI config and set it: sentinel-dvpn config init # ~/.sentinel-dvpn/config.toml [rpc] url = "<SOLANA_RPC_URL>" ws_url = "<SOLANA_WS_URL>" Check the result: sentinel-dvpn config show
documents.s: 3. Get SOL and check the RPC endpoint

documents.t: sentinel-dvpn wallet balance sentinel-dvpn wallet create-token-account sentinel-dvpn wallet approve-delegate --amount-base-units <BOUNDED_BASE_UNITS> approve-delegate lets the program move dVPN tokens for your payments. Use a bounded amount in base units. unlimited also works, but a bounded amount limits the exposure. revoke-delegate removes the allowance.

Client instance tags start with c: sudo sentinel-dvpnd init --instance c0 --owner <OWNER_PUBLIC_KEY> Save the public_key value from the output. The client daemon signs channel transactions with that key, so fund it with SOL too.

Init encrypts the daemon key by default. The daemon never prompts, so create a passphrase file and point the client config at it, as in Save the passphrase: # /var/lib/sentinel-dvpn/c0/config.toml [key] name = "operator" passphrase_file = "/etc/sentinel-dvpn/c0.pass" Run it in the foreground for a first test: sudo sentinel-dvpnd run --instance c0 To run it as a service, use sudo sentinel-dvpnd service install --instance c0, then service start --instance c0. Check that the CLI can reach it. Daemon commands take --instance: sentinel-dvpn daemon status --instance c0 Next: connect to a node.
documents.s: 6. Set the passphrase and run the daemon

documents.t: The dvpn Anchor program holds the on-chain state for the Sentinel dVPN protocol on Solana. Draft Instruction and account names come from the program's IDL, sentinel-programs/idl/dvpn.json in sentinel-solana. The IDL and declare_id! (in sentinel-programs/programs/dvpn/src/lib.rs) use the localnet placeholder SentineLDVPN1111111111111111111111111111111. The devnet deployment uses the program ID below.

Item Address Program ID J52dyXW3a6mkatvrQct3fo6dA9vqUtcsdBt5gGqrTBXs Config account (PDA, seed config) Cu5vofxVQgZXRVwfBqApw84ZWy1hjhDmHkznyDr6TRiQ dVPN token mint (Token-2022) Hen2LVP6KooGaXEvdSyCHWghsEY4gLLn7wix8z6zHFSa Vault EQJyAyWLGZSye3BMfDQVdhrfp1QKEByNX9q2J9TzFmfy Treasury token account Gej7quWtz869TiidkTjrm7yer7EnR8yE82TGEyHdmDYr The mint, vault, and treasury come from the program's on-chain Config account.

Account Holds Config Program parameters, including the minimum node bond, treasury, mint, vault, and the pause mask. User A user's balance. Node A node's owner, status, prices, protocols, country, URI, bond, revenue, accrued protocol fees, and rent recipient. NodeUnbonding Bond held while a closed node is unbonding. Provider A provider's owner, bond, and revenue. ProviderUnbonding Bond held while a closed provider is unbonding. Plan A subscription plan offered by a provider. Grant Permission a granter gives a grantee to act on a target, with an optional spending allowance and expiry. Subscription A user's subscription to a plan. Lease A user's lease of a node, by voucher or stream. Channel A user's payment channel with a node, by voucher or stream.
Grants carry a bit mask. These are the node permissions: Permission Value Update node 2 (1 << 1) List node 4 (1 << 2) Delist node 8 (1 << 3)

Config and governance initialize_config, set_params, set_paused_mask, set_treasury, propose_authority, accept_authority, sweep_config_fees Nodes open_node, update_node, list_node, delist_node, sweep_node_fees, close_node, withdraw_node_bond, withdraw_node_revenue Providers open_provider, update_provider, list_provider, delist_provider, close_provider, sweep_provider_fees, withdraw_provider_bond, withdraw_provider_revenue, withdraw_provider_balance Plans open_plan, update_plan, list_plan, delist_plan, close_plan Grants open_grant, update_grant, close_grant Subscriptions open_subscription, close_subscription Leases open_lease, fund_leases, redeem_lease_vouchers, redeem_lease_streams, start_close_lease, close_lease Channels open_channel, fund_channels, redeem_channel_vouchers, redeem_channel_streams, start_close_channel, close_channel Users withdraw_user_balance For how to call these from the command line, see Node Operators and Clients.
Run a Sentinel dVPN node that is registered and paid on Solana (devnet).

A new Linux server (Ubuntu 26.04, x86_64) with a public IP. Your own computer (Linux or macOS), to hold the owner key. Devnet SOL from the Solana faucet, and tDVPN for the bond. The devnet tDVPN source is TBD.
Key Where it lives What it does Owner Your computer Owns the node, pays the bond, receives revenue. Keep it off the server. Operator The server Runs the node. Needs a little SOL for fees.

Prepare Your Computer: install the CLI and create the owner key. Prepare the Server: install the software. Configure the Node: create the node's config and operator key. Register the Node On-Chain: open the node and grant the operator key. Start the Node: open the firewall, check, and run it. Manage the Node: change settings, update, reinstall, withdraw, shut down. One node runs one protocol. For each extra node on the same server, repeat steps 3–5.
Run these commands on your computer (Linux or macOS), not on the server. The owner key lives here.
Install git, make, and Go 1.27.3.

cd ~ git clone https://github.com/sentinel-official/sentinel-solana.git cd ~/sentinel-solana make -C sentinel-dvpn build \ SENTINEL_NETWORK=devnet \ SENTINEL_PROGRAM_ID=J52dyXW3a6mkatvrQct3fo6dA9vqUtcsdBt5gGqrTBXs \ SENTINEL_MINT=Hen2LVP6KooGaXEvdSyCHWghsEY4gLLn7wix8z6zHFSa sudo install -m 755 sentinel-dvpn/bin/sentinel-dvpn /usr/local/bin/ sentinel-dvpn version The output must show "network":"devnet".

New key (it asks for a passphrase): sentinel-dvpn key new owner Or use a key file you already have (a Solana keypair JSON): cd <FOLDER_WITH_OWNER_JSON> install -d -m 700 ~/.sentinel-dvpn/keys install -m 600 owner.json ~/.sentinel-dvpn/keys/owner.json Print its public key. The next pages call it <OWNER_PUBLIC_KEY>: sentinel-dvpn key show owner Back up ~/.sentinel-dvpn/keys/owner.json (and its passphrase) somewhere safe.

SOL: get devnet SOL for <OWNER_PUBLIC_KEY> from the Solana faucet. tDVPN: each node needs a bond. The examples use 10 tDVPN per node. The devnet tDVPN source is TBD. Create the token account, then check the balance: sentinel-dvpn wallet create-token-account sentinel-dvpn wallet balance dvpn_base_units is your tDVPN. 1 tDVPN = 1,000,000. Next: prepare the server.
Steps marked computer use the owner key. Run them on your computer. Steps marked server run on the server.

Server. The server's config wins: every 5 minutes, the node copies the prices, country, URI, and protocol it loaded at start to the chain. Change them in the config, not with update-node. Edit the config. Prices are in the [prices] section. 1 tDVPN = 1,000,000. sudoedit /var/lib/sentinel-dvpn/n0/config.toml Restart. The node pushes the change to the chain right away. sudo sentinel-dvpnd service restart --instance n0 If you changed a port, open it in the firewall (Start, step 1).

Server. cd ~/sentinel-solana git pull for dir in sentinel-dvpn sentinel-dvpnd; do make -C "$dir" build \ SENTINEL_NETWORK=devnet \ SENTINEL_PROGRAM_ID=J52dyXW3a6mkatvrQct3fo6dA9vqUtcsdBt5gGqrTBXs \ SENTINEL_MINT=Hen2LVP6KooGaXEvdSyCHWghsEY4gLLn7wix8z6zHFSa done sudo install -m 755 sentinel-dvpn/bin/sentinel-dvpn sentinel-dvpnd/bin/sentinel-dvpnd /usr/local/bin/ sudo sentinel-dvpnd service restart --instance n0 Run the last line once for every node (n0, n1, …).

Use this if the server was wiped but the node is still on-chain. You keep the node, its grant, and its revenue. You need the operator key backup from Configure, step 5. Computer. Find the node's node_id, port (end of uri), and protocols: sentinel-dvpn node search --owner <OWNER_PUBLIC_KEY> Server. Do Prepare the Server. Do Configure the Node. In step 2, copy in your operator key backup. In step 3, use the same --service and --api-port as before. Server. Replace the new id with the old node_id: sudo sed -i "s/^id = '.*'/id = '<OLD_NODE_ID>'/" /var/lib/sentinel-dvpn/n0/config.toml Do Start the Node. Skip Register: the node and grant are still on-chain.
Computer. sentinel-dvpn node show <NODE_ADDRESS> sentinel-dvpn node withdraw-node-revenue --node <NODE_ADDRESS> --amount <BASE_UNITS> revenue in the show output is what you can withdraw.

Do the steps in this order. A running node lists itself again, and it can't claim payments after the node is closed. Server. Claim what clients owe. Payments under 10 tDVPN can be claimed once they are 1 hour old, so run this at least 1 hour after the last client session. sudo sentinel-dvpn node redeem --instance n0 Server. Stop and remove the service: sudo sentinel-dvpnd service uninstall --instance n0 Computer. Close the node. This pays out the revenue and starts unbonding the bond: sentinel-dvpn node close-node --node <NODE_ADDRESS> Computer. Wait unbonding_seconds (see sentinel-dvpn program params). Then find the unbonding address and withdraw the bond: sentinel-dvpn node unbonding search --owner <OWNER_PUBLIC_KEY> sentinel-dvpn node withdraw-node-bond --node-unbonding <UNBONDING_ADDRESS> Computer. Close the grant to get its rent back. Use the grant address whose target is the node: sentinel-dvpn grant search --granter <OWNER_PUBLIC_KEY> sentinel-dvpn grant close-grant --grant <GRANT_ADDRESS> Server. Delete the node's files (this deletes the operator key, so keep your backup): sudo rm -rf /var/lib/sentinel-dvpn/n0 /etc/sentinel-dvpn/n0.pass

Run these commands on your computer, not on the server. They use the owner key from Prepare Your Computer. You need id and public_key from Configure the Node. public_key is the operator key; the steps call it <OPERATOR_PUBLIC_KEY>. tip If a command fails with 429 or rate limits exceeded, wait a few seconds and run it again.
The operator key pays the node's fees. Get devnet SOL for <OPERATOR_PUBLIC_KEY> from the Solana faucet, for example 0.1 SOL. Check it: sentinel-dvpn wallet balance --owner <OPERATOR_PUBLIC_KEY>

Use the same country, port, and prices as init. sentinel-dvpn node open-node \ --node-id <ID_FROM_INIT> \ --country <COUNTRY_CODE> \ --uri "https://<SERVER_IP>:8443" \ --protocols 1 \ --bond 10000000 \ --prices.channel-price-per-gb 50000000 \ --prices.channel-price-per-hour 50000000 \ --prices.lease-price-per-hour 50000000 --protocols is the number for the node's protocol: Protocol --protocols wireguard 1 v2ray 2 openvpn 4 amneziawg 8 xray 16 hysteria2 32 --bond is in base units (10000000 = 10 tDVPN). It must be at least min_node_bond from sentinel-dvpn program params.
sentinel-dvpn node search --owner <OWNER_PUBLIC_KEY> Copy the address of the entry whose node_id matches your id. The next steps call it <NODE_ADDRESS>.

sentinel-dvpn grant open-grant \ --grantee <OPERATOR_PUBLIC_KEY> \ --target <NODE_ADDRESS> \ --permissions 6 \ --never-expires \ --allowance 0 6 lets the server update and list the node. --allowance 0 means it can't spend your tokens.
documents.s: 4. Let the operator key run the node

documents.t: sentinel-dvpn node show <NODE_ADDRESS> Check the uri, protocols, and prices. The node lists itself for clients when you start it. Next: start the node.
Run every command on this page on the server. Written for a new Ubuntu 26.04 (x86_64) server.
A new server gives you root. From your computer: ssh root@<SERVER_IP>

Skip this step if you already have one. Pick a name for <USER>. adduser asks for a password. adduser <USER> usermod -aG sudo <USER> install -d -m 700 -o <USER> -g <USER> /home/<USER>/.ssh install -m 600 -o <USER> -g <USER> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys /home/<USER>/.ssh/authorized_keys exit If you log in to root with a password instead of an SSH key, skip the two install lines. Log back in as the new user. Run every step after this as that user. ssh <USER>@<SERVER_IP>

Do this if the server has 2 GB of RAM or less. Without it, the build can run out of memory. Skip it if swapon --show already prints a line. sudo fallocate -l 2G /swapfile sudo chmod 600 /swapfile sudo mkswap /swapfile sudo swapon /swapfile echo "/swapfile none swap sw 0 0" | sudo tee -a /etc/fstab
sudo apt-get update sudo apt-get install -y ca-certificates curl git unzip build-essential wireguard-tools openvpn nftables

cd /tmp curl -fsSLo go.tgz https://go.dev/dl/go1.27.3.linux-amd64.tar.gz echo "65efbc80fdc1fa2cd2631cad5b481777a68e8725f34e89f50fc6ac714e379b40 go.tgz" | sha256sum -c - && \ sudo rm -rf /usr/local/go && \ sudo tar -C /usr/local -xzf go.tgz && \ sudo ln -sf /usr/local/go/bin/go /usr/local/bin/go rm -f go.tgz go version If sha256sum doesn't print go.tgz: OK, nothing is installed. Run the block again. On many servers /tmp is too small for the build. Make Go use a folder in your home instead: mkdir -p "${HOME}/go-tmp" go env -w GOTMPDIR="${HOME}/go-tmp"

On a 1-CPU server this takes about 15 minutes. cd ~ git clone https://github.com/sentinel-official/sentinel-solana.git cd ~/sentinel-solana for dir in sentinel-dvpn sentinel-dvpnd; do make -C "$dir" build \ SENTINEL_NETWORK=devnet \ SENTINEL_PROGRAM_ID=J52dyXW3a6mkatvrQct3fo6dA9vqUtcsdBt5gGqrTBXs \ SENTINEL_MINT=Hen2LVP6KooGaXEvdSyCHWghsEY4gLLn7wix8z6zHFSa done sudo install -m 755 sentinel-dvpn/bin/sentinel-dvpn sentinel-dvpnd/bin/sentinel-dvpnd /usr/local/bin/ sentinel-dvpnd version The output must show "network":"devnet".
