documents.t: Each node runs one protocol. Install only what your nodes need. In each block, if sha256sum doesn't print OK, nothing is installed. Run the block again.
Nothing to do. Step 4 installed it.
Nothing to do. Step 4 installed it.

Needs V2Ray 5. Don't use apt install v2ray: Ubuntu ships V2Ray 4, which doesn't work. cd /tmp curl -fsSLo v2ray.zip https://github.com/v2fly/v2ray-core/releases/download/v5.53.0/v2ray-linux-64.zip echo "6bbb8aee65a57d0b12599b4b7c842b3ad0daca4436e661d94015c447cb31b4fa v2ray.zip" | sha256sum -c - && \ unzip -oqj v2ray.zip v2ray && \ sudo install -m 755 v2ray /usr/local/bin/v2ray rm -f v2ray v2ray.zip v2ray version

cd /tmp curl -fsSLo xray.zip https://github.com/XTLS/Xray-core/releases/download/v26.3.27/Xray-linux-64.zip echo "23cd9af937744d97776ee35ecad4972cf4b2109d1e0fe6be9930467608f7c8ae xray.zip" | sha256sum -c - && \ unzip -oqj xray.zip xray && \ sudo install -m 755 xray /usr/local/bin/xray rm -f xray xray.zip xray version

The file must be named hysteria2. cd /tmp curl -fsSLo hysteria2 https://github.com/apernet/hysteria/releases/download/app/v2.9.2/hysteria-linux-amd64 echo "86fef8e2f1b2bf41318ac96724eee6c3b449e4e510022cc89658b63a6713922a hysteria2" | sha256sum -c - && \ sudo install -m 755 hysteria2 /usr/local/bin/hysteria2 rm -f hysteria2 hysteria2 version

Needs two parts: the awg tools and amneziawg-go. cd /tmp git clone https://github.com/amnezia-vpn/amneziawg-tools.git git -C amneziawg-tools checkout 61e741780e8465a67a7d7fb6cffe14a8a15d624a make -C amneziawg-tools/src make -C amneziawg-tools/src install DESTDIR=/tmp/awg-out PREFIX=/usr \ WITH_WGQUICK=yes WITH_BASHCOMPLETION=no WITH_SYSTEMDUNITS=no sudo install -m 755 /tmp/awg-out/usr/bin/awg /tmp/awg-out/usr/bin/awg-quick /usr/local/bin/ git clone https://github.com/amnezia-vpn/amneziawg-go.git git -C amneziawg-go checkout 1cc94272ca8e9e223a5fe76382f5880f09d3c12d (cd amneziawg-go && go build -o amneziawg-go .) sudo install -m 755 amneziawg-go/amneziawg-go /usr/local/bin/amneziawg-go rm -rf amneziawg-tools amneziawg-go /tmp/awg-out awg --version Next: configure the node.
Run these commands on the server, unless a step says on your computer. Finish Prepare the Server first.

Each node is one instance with one protocol. Give each instance its own tag (n0, n1, …) and its own API port. Tag Protocol (--service) API port n0 wireguard 8443 n1 amneziawg 8444 n2 v2ray 8445 n3 xray 8446 n4 openvpn 8447 n5 hysteria2 8448 The examples below use n0, wireguard, and 8443.
documents.s: 1. Pick a tag, a protocol, and a port

documents.t: Skip this step to let init create a new key. To use a key file you already have (a backup from step 5, or a Solana keypair JSON), copy it in before init. On your computer: cd <FOLDER_WITH_OPERATOR_JSON> scp operator.json <USER>@<SERVER_IP>:~/operator.json On the server: sudo install -d -m 700 /var/lib/sentinel-dvpn/n0/keys sudo install -m 600 ~/operator.json /var/lib/sentinel-dvpn/n0/keys/operator.json rm ~/operator.json

<OWNER_PUBLIC_KEY> comes from Prepare Your Computer. Prices are in base units: 1 tDVPN = 1,000,000. The example sets every price to 50 tDVPN. sudo sentinel-dvpnd init \ --instance n0 \ --owner <OWNER_PUBLIC_KEY> \ --country <COUNTRY_CODE> \ --api-hosts <SERVER_IP> \ --api-port 8443 \ --service wireguard \ --prices.channel-per-gb 50000000 \ --prices.channel-per-hour 50000000 \ --prices.lease-per-hour 50000000 <COUNTRY_CODE>: two capital letters, for example SG. Write down id and public_key from the output. You need them on-chain. If init asks for a passphrase, choose one for a new key, or type your key file's passphrase. Then do step 4.

Skip this step if init didn't ask for a passphrase. sudo mkdir -p /etc/sentinel-dvpn sudo install -m 600 /dev/null /etc/sentinel-dvpn/n0.pass sudoedit /etc/sentinel-dvpn/n0.pass Type the passphrase. To save in nano, press Ctrl+O, Enter, then Ctrl+X. Point the config at the file: sudo sed -i "s|^passphrase_file = ''|passphrase_file = '/etc/sentinel-dvpn/n0.pass'|" /var/lib/sentinel-dvpn/n0/config.toml

You need this file to reinstall the node later. On the server: sudo install -m 600 -o "$USER" /var/lib/sentinel-dvpn/n0/keys/operator.json ~/operator-n0.json On your computer: cd <FOLDER_FOR_BACKUPS> scp <USER>@<SERVER_IP>:~/operator-n0.json . On the server: rm ~/operator-n0.json If init asked for a passphrase, keep it with the backup.

sudo sed -i '/^\[speedtest\]$/,/^\[/ s/^enabled = true$/enabled = false/' /var/lib/sentinel-dvpn/n0/config.toml sudo grep -A1 '^\[speedtest\]' /var/lib/sentinel-dvpn/n0/config.toml The output must show enabled = false.

The public devnet RPC limits requests. With several nodes, your own RPC avoids 429 errors. sudo sed -i \ -e "s|^url = 'https://api.devnet.solana.com'|url = '<RPC_URL>'|" \ -e "s|^ws_url = 'wss://api.devnet.solana.com'|ws_url = '<WS_URL>'|" \ /var/lib/sentinel-dvpn/n0/config.toml Next: register the node on-chain.
Run these commands on the server. Finish Register the Node On-Chain first. The node can't start without its grant.

Skip this step if sudo ufw status prints Status: inactive and your cloud provider has no firewall. Find the VPN ports in the protocol's config file: sudo cat /var/lib/sentinel-dvpn/n0/wireguard/config.toml Protocol Ports to open wireguard, amneziawg, hysteria2 listen_port, UDP openvpn listen_port, using its protocol (udp or tcp) v2ray, xray every port under [[inbounds]], TCP Leave the other ports in the file closed. Open the API port, then each VPN port. <PROTO> is udp or tcp from the table. sudo ufw allow 8443/tcp sudo ufw allow <VPN_PORT>/<PROTO> Add the same ports to your cloud provider's firewall, if it has one.

Run this before you start the node: sudo sentinel-dvpnd doctor --instance n0 --output table Every row must show ok. Fix any that don't, then run it again. While the node is running, api_port always shows error.
sudo sentinel-dvpnd service install --instance n0 sudo sentinel-dvpnd service start --instance n0 The service also starts on every reboot.

sudo sentinel-dvpnd service status --instance n0 sudo sentinel-dvpn node status --instance n0 To watch the logs (press Ctrl+C to stop): sudo journalctl -u sentinel-dvpnd@n0 -f The log shows service started when the VPN is up.
For each extra node, repeat Configure, Register, and Start. Use the next tag (n1, n2, …), that node's protocol, and its own API port.
